newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina may change Falklands Day for Japan emperor.
newsitem.headline: Argentina may change Falklands Day for Japan emperor.

text.p: Argentina's tourist industry was up in arms on Wednesday over a proposal to change a national holiday marking the claim to sovereignty of the Falkland Islands because of a visit by the Japanese emperor.
The government wants to move the holiday to June 13 from June 9 to avoid having Buenos Aires look like a ghost town during an official visit by Emperor Akihito.

"A national policy which puts an official visit by Japan's emperor above the interests of the community is inexplicable," said the Association of Travel Agents, fearing cancellations by Argentines who had been planning long-weekend trips.

The Right to Sovereignty of the Malvinas Day -- Malvinas being the Argentine name for the islands -- has been marked on the national calendar since Argentina and Britain clashed in 1982 in a 10-week war over the South Atlantic territory.
Argentina lost the war but maintains its claim to the islands, which it says were usurped by Britain in 1833.
The government, which will put the proposal to Congress on Wednesday to change the national holiday just this year, argues that foreign policy considerations justify its move.
Emperor Akihito arrives on June 9 for a three day visit to meet with government officials and members of the Japanese community.
